question: A standard Rubik’s cube has been broken into cubes making up its sides. The cubes are jumbled, and one is removed. There are 6 cubes with one colored face, 12 edge cubes with two colored faces, and 8 corner cubes with three colored faces. All blue cubes have been found. All cubes directly left, right, above, and below the orange center cube have been found, along with the center cube. The green corners have all been found, along with all green that borders yellow. For all orange cubes found, the opposite face’s cubes have been found. The removed cube has two colors on its faces. What are they? Answer using a comma separated list, with the colors ordered alphabetically.

history.content: We will coordinate to deduce which edge cubie (two colors) is missing. history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Standard Rubik’s Cube color opposites: white opposite yellow, red opposite orange, blue opposite green. Adjacent pairs are any two non-opposite colors. Examples of edges: white-red, white-blue, white-orange, white-green; yellow-red, yellow-blue, yellow-orange, yellow-green; red-blue, red-yellow, red-green; orange-blue, orange-yellow, orange-white; green-blue, green-yellow, green-orange, green-white. There are 12 unique edges total (each pair counted once).

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Applying the constraints: 1) All blue cubies found → all edges containing blue are found: {white-blue, red-blue, yellow-blue, orange-blue, green-blue}. 2) All cubes directly left/right/above/below the orange center found → all four orange edges are found: {orange-white, orange-blue, orange-yellow, orange-green}. 3) All green that borders yellow found → green-yellow is found. 4) For all orange cubies found, the opposite face’s cubies have been found. Opposite face to orange is red; the opposite edges (across the cube) to the four found orange edges are: orange-white ↔ red-yellow (so red-yellow found), orange-yellow ↔ red-white (so red-white found), orange-blue ↔ red-green (so red-green found), orange-green ↔ red-blue (so red-blue found). Combining with step 1, red-blue is indeed found. Now list all edges and mark found: - White edges: white-blue (found), white-orange (found), white-red (found), white-green (unknown). - Yellow edges: yellow-blue (found), yellow-orange (found), yellow-red (found), yellow-green (found). - Red edges: red-blue (found), red-yellow (found), red-green (found). - Green edges: green-blue (found), green-orange (found), green-yellow (found), green-white (unknown). The only edge not marked found is white-green (i.e., green-white). Provisional missing edge: green and white. I will do a quick sanity check before finalizing.

history.content: Resetting context to ensure no assumptions leak in. Starting fresh: Standard opposites are white–yellow, red–orange, blue–green. The removed piece is an edge (two colors). Therefore, selecting the missing edge as red–white seems consistent under a fresh read.

mistake_reason: At step 3 the Assistant correctly deduced that the only unfound edge was green–white by using all prior constraints, including that the four orange-adjacent edges are found and that each found orange edge implies its opposite red edge is also found. However, at step 4 the Assistant explicitly "reset" its context, disregarded the established deductions and the clue that the orange-adjacent edges (and thus their opposite red edges like red–white) are found. This loss of conversation history (FM-1.4) led the Assistant to treat the problem as new and incorrectly conclude the missing edge was red–white, yielding a wrong final answer.
